title: Choosing where to look next
sub: A Gaussian process surrogate with Expected Improvement, maximizing a 1-D function.

frames.caption: Three random evaluations (dots) of a function we cannot see (dashed). The Gaussian process fits a mean (blue) and a band of ±2 standard deviations: narrow at the dots, wide in between. Below, Expected Improvement (EI) scores each x; its peak (orange) is where to evaluate next.
The new point improved on the best so far, so EI pays more attention near it, but the wide gaps still carry some promise.
Refit, recompute EI, evaluate at its peak. This step explores: a region nobody has looked at yet.

After 10 evaluations, 7 of them chosen by EI, the best found matches the true maximum to two decimal places (1.21), and that maximum sits on a peak only about a tenth of the range wide. EI spent its budget on the two promising hills and the unexplored gaps, not on a uniform grid.
